notes.what_this_is: The register of ACCEPTED numeric movements for scripts/impact_report.py. An entry is a recorded decision that a number moved and that the new figure is right - the same preserve-or-fix convention the reporting goldens and the supervisory validation register use. It is NOT a waiver: `compare` exits non-zero on any movement that has no entry here.
notes.when_to_add_an_entry: Only after you have established WHY the figure moved and that the NEW figure is correct. If you cannot write that sentence, the movement is a defect, not an entry.
notes.when_to_remove_an_entry: As soon as the movement it accounts for is in the new baseline. An entry survives exactly one baseline refresh: once the baseline is re-captured, the movement is gone and the entry is stale. Run `compare --stale-check` to find entries that no longer match anything.

entry_shape.grain: one of: total | class | cell | error
entry_shape.key: the '|'-joined coordinate exactly as the report prints it; see key_fields below
entry_shape.reason: free text, mandatory - at least 20 characters and 4 words, and not a placeholder. Say what moved and why the new number is right, with the regulatory or code reason.
entry_shape.accepted_under: the commit sha or PR number the decision was taken under

notes.wildcards: A key containing *, ? or [ is matched with fnmatch. Wildcards are permitted because a legitimate change can move thousands of cells at once, but they widen silently - the report prints how many movements each entry matched, so a wildcard's blast radius is always visible. Prefer the narrowest pattern that covers the change.

example_entry_do_not_treat_as_live.reason: Art. 111 CCF schedule change under PS1/26 raises the undrawn conversion factor from 20% to 40% for this bucket, so the exposure value rises; verified by hand against PS1/26 Table A1 and against tests/acceptance/basel31/test_p1_111_ccf.py.
